title: Platform Geometry
description: Geometrical information about a specific platform.

platform_type.description: Type of platform. `vessel` is a craft whose sensors are mounted on a hull. `sensor_station` is a fixed or pier-mounted sensor installation (a mast, tower or quayside rig) whose sensors are surveyed against a site. `operator_station` is a place from which platforms are monitored or operated, such as a remote operations centre.

ccrp_m.title: CCRP
ccrp_m.description: Consistent Common Reference Point position in the platform local coordinate system (X forward, Y starboard, Z down).

mmsi_number.description: Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI) number. Used for AIS identification.

imo_number.description: IMO ship identification number. Use 0 if not assigned (e.g. small craft).

call_sign.description: Radio call sign assigned to this platform.

operational_limits.title: Operational Limits
operational_limits.description: Operational envelope of this platform. Used by supervision and mission planning systems.

vessel_outlines.title: Vessel Outlines
vessel_outlines.description: Named hull cross-section polygons in body-frame coordinates (meters relative to CCRP). Keys are outline names (e.g. complex_max, waterline, above_waterline_1m). Coordinate convention: X = forward (bow), Y = starboard.

description.description: Human-readable label for this outline cross-section.

coordinates_m.description: Closed polygon ring of [x_forward_m, y_starboard_m] points relative to CCRP.

sensor_type.description: Type of sensor mounted at this frame (optional, for service discovery and visualization).

sensor_description.description: Human-readable label for the sensor at this frame.

translation_m.title: Translation
translation_m.description: A translation in meters of the child frame in relation to the parent frame expressed in the parent frame of reference.

rotation_deg.title: Rotation
rotation_deg.description: A rotation in degrees of the child frame in relation to the parent frame expressed in the parent frame of reference given as Euler angles applied in the order YAW -> PITCH -> ROLL

payloads.title: Payloads
payloads.description: The payloads this platform carries -- gimbals, winches, cranes, sonars, samplers, launchers -- one entry each. Each is held under its own PAYLOAD_AUTHORITY lease (command_authority, slot {vessel_id}/payload/{id}) and driven over payload_control/v1 by its own connector and payload gate, never as a motion degree of freedom (protocols/payload_control.yaml). Each `id` is the name it goes by on the bus.

id.description: Unique on this platform, and a single key chunk -- e.g. `gimbal`, `crane-1`.

kind.description: What the payload is. The kind suggests the safe state (camera_gimbal HOLD_POSITION, winch BRAKE_HOLD, crane HOLD_LOAD, towed sonar HOLD_WINCH, sampler RETRACT_OR_HOLD, launcher INHIBIT), but the policy below is what decides.

axes.description: The payload's axes, each addressed `<axis>/<id>` on payload_control/v1 (keelson#327's naming).

id.description: The axis, a single key chunk -- e.g. `pan`, `tilt`, `slew`, `hoist`.

affects_stability.description: Moving it changes the ship's stability (a crane under load). It then moves only under the conn holder's payload_clearance.

affects_navigation.description: Deploying it limits how the ship may be navigated (a towed sonar). It then moves only under the conn holder's payload_clearance.

payload_safe_state_policy.description: What the payload gate does on a lost lease, the dead-man, a broken clearance or the local lockout. "Idle" is not one of them: it is the wrong answer for a crane with a load on the hook.

command_profile.description: Who may RESET the emergency stop and what a missing safety supervisor means (protocols/emergency_request.yaml). `operational`: OVERALL_COMMAND only, and no new remote-control arming without the supervisor. `test` and `legacy_single_operator`: the CONN holder, and a missing supervisor is an alarm. Safety-relevant: changed only through maintenance_state (protocols/command_authority.yaml), never live by an operator.

safety_independence.description: How independent the safety path is: L1 its own process and Zenoh session, L2 its own network path, L3 its own compute, L4 its own power, L5 a physical PLC or relay in the actuator circuit. Two sessions on one router on one box is L1, and nothing here claims more. Safety-relevant: changed only through maintenance_state (protocols/command_authority.yaml), never live by an operator.

responsible_roc.description: The default responsible ROC site the authority manager starts from (OVERALL_COMMAND's record carries the live one). Safety-relevant: changed only through maintenance_state (protocols/command_authority.yaml), never live by an operator.

active_control_station.description: The default active control station: the site whose hands are on the helm when nothing has moved it. Safety-relevant: changed only through maintenance_state (protocols/command_authority.yaml), never live by an operator.

control_matrix.description: Per vehicle mode and per DOF: the eligible sources, the active one, the fallback, and the DOFs that move together. The motion gate (protocols/control_gate.yaml) reads it. Safety-relevant: changed only through maintenance_state (protocols/command_authority.yaml), never live by an operator.

modes.description: Every mode the fault table names.

safety_trip.description: Who holds SAFETY_TRIP, the right to stop the ship. Humans default to yes, processes to no; every process granted it is named here.

safe_state_policy.description: What each loss does, per mode, the watchdog that trips it, and the timeouts. Only an onboard component trips a fallback; the ROC alarms. Safety-relevant: changed only through maintenance_state (protocols/command_authority.yaml), never live by an operator.

hold.description: What `HOLD` is on this vessel: loiter on her current position, neutral, or a local controller keeping heading and speed.

transition_state.description: The state the gate enters on Abort automation, a lapsed CONN or no committed map, per mode. Never an implicit "nobody".

faults.description: One row per loss. A row names the watchdog that trips it: a row without one is a wish.

on_safety_supervisor_loss_while_active.description: What a vessel already underway does when the safety supervisor's liveliness token goes, per mode.

supervisor_loss_continue_for_s.description: How long CONTINUE_FOR continues, in seconds. Required when any mode of on_safety_supervisor_loss_while_active is CONTINUE_FOR.

timeouts.description: Watchdog timeouts in seconds, judged on the receiver's monotonic clock. The clearance binding is checked every cycle and has none.

hid_read_s.description: Physical device: the HID read watchdog, after which the device is DEGRADED. Default 0.1.

candidate_invalid_s.description: Candidate stream: freshness after which the candidate is INVALID. Default 0.5-1.0.

control_link_s.description: Control link (CONTROL_LINK_HEALTH): the commanding station's input reaching the gate. Default 2.

conn_manual_lease_s.description: CONN lease TTL under manual control. Default 2.

conn_conduct_lease_s.description: CONN lease TTL under conduct (a navigation process holds it). Default 30.

session_lease_s.description: Session lease TTL of the human assignments (OVERALL, NAVIGATIONAL). Default 30.

navigation_holder_s.description: A human navigation-function holder's lease. Default 30.

succession_policy.description: Who may ASSUME_COMMAND for an unreachable OVERALL_COMMAND or NAVIGATIONAL_COMMAND assignee. The record always carries the reason, the evidence and an audit event (protocols/command_authority.yaml). An empty `deputies` refuses every assumption. Safety-relevant: changed only through maintenance_state (protocols/command_authority.yaml), never live by an operator.

navigation_functions.description: Per navigation function, the highest SARUMS control method NAVIGATION_AUTHORITY may grant the navigator (1 Manual ... 5 Autonomous), and what silence means for it under method 3 and above. Safety-relevant: changed only through maintenance_state (protocols/command_authority.yaml), never live by an operator.

fault_actions.description: What the vessel does, per mode.

watchdog.description: The watchdog that trips this row.

dofs.description: Keyed by DOF, as vehicle_control/v1 names its axes: `steering`, `throttle`, `thruster/<id>`, `propeller_pitch`.

eligible_sources.description: Source classes the gate resolves to a producer: the active control station's helm, the navigation process, the vessel's own autopilot.

fallback.description: Where the DOF goes when its active source is lost: another source, or HOLD / NEUTRAL.

coupled.description: Groups of DOFs that change source together, one ControlMapping.group_id each.
